messages:
elaine: FYI customer "BetaBank" is pushing for a timeline to migrate from our old prompt param to a messages-first shape. they need two features: a pinned system persona that cannot be overridden, and deterministic JSON responses for payments routing. can we scope this Q2?

rafa: quick take 1: messages-first is straightforward to accept server-side. the sticky bit is the "pinned persona" semantics across hosted/dedicated/private and ensuring RBAC prevents overrides.

kevin (eng): implementation thought: add a tenant-level "pinned_system" record; requests can include a system entry but we merge and reject if it conflicts when tenant.pinned_system.enforced == true. merge rule: pinned takes precedence and is prepended.

nina (solutions): BetaBank also asked that function outputs strictly match their JSON schema; they want invalid responses blocked and surfaced as actionable errors to their app. they also asked for a migration checklist.

tom (sdk): SDK impact: will need helper that converts old prompt -> messages and warns about system role conflicts. also add helpers for parsing function_call payloads and schema validation helpers. estimated 10 dev days across py/js.

elaine: launch gates we should require: 1) messages+prompt alias accepted by API, 2) pinned persona config + enforcement for dedicated/private and opt-in on hosted, 3) function-calling + schema validation modes (strict/log-only), 4) example SDK migrations, 5) evals show no material regression in safety/accuracy, 6) docs + migration checklist.

kevin (eng): schema validation modes proposal:
- strict: server validates response against provided JSON Schema; on mismatch, return error 422 and no assistant text.
- soft-log: server returns assistant text but flags response with header + telemetry counter.
- fixup: attempt to coerce/repair (parse strings to JSON, type casts) then return repaired payload + inspection metadata.

nina: BetaBank wants strict by default for their tenant. are we comfortable exposing per-tenant defaults?

rafa: yes but gated: hosted default = soft-log to avoid breaks for small apps. Dedicated/private can set tenant.default_schema_mode = strict. ops challenge: strict mode will increase error rates during rollout; we need migration tooling.

tom (sdk): example request sketch (for docs):
```json
{
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"You are a payments assistant. DO NOT reveal PII."},
    {"role":"user","content":"route $120 to vendor X"}
  ],
  "functions": [
    {"name":"routePayment","description":"routes payments","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"amount":{"type":"number"},"vendor":{"type":"string"}},"required":["amount","vendor"]}}
  ],
  "schema_mode":"strict"
}
```

kevin (eng): runtime behavior for strict: we validate the function_call.arguments against schema; if invalid, we return a structured error with fields: {code, message, validation_errors}. Also increment tenant.metrics.schema_rejections. We should include a header x-rw-schema-status: rejected|accepted|fixed.

nina: UX ask: provide a console view that shows schema rejections and example failing outputs. even if console UI is v2, at least expose the telemetry endpoints for now.

elaine: canary plan: 1) internal E2E, 2) SDKs + docs, 3) hosted canary (2% traffic) with soft-log default, 4) onboard BetaBank to dedicated sandbox with strict mode, 5) monitor for 1 week then expand.

rafa: rough timeline: core runtime changes 3w, SDKs 2w (parallel), docs + migration guide 1w, canary ops 1w. resource ask: 2 backend, 1 infra, 1 SDK, .5 QA.

kevin (eng): QA needs a schema-violation harness and synthetic traffic generator to emulate common failure modes (truncated tokens, partial JSON, float vs string). add to CI matrix.

tom (sdk): also add a migration CLI that will scan existing apps for prompt usage and provide a suggested messages mapping and a list of potential system-role conflicts. small tool we can ship as alpha.

nina: for customer comms: I'll draft BetaBank proposal that includes the strict mode opt-in, example requests, expected error shapes, and recommended migration steps.

elaine: acceptance criteria checklist (draft):
- API accepts messages array + backward-compatible prompt alias
- tenant.pinned_system exists and is enforceable; enforcement documented
- function calling supports JSON Schema parameters and server-side validation modes (strict/soft-log/fixup)
- SDKs (py/js) include prompt->messages helpers and schema validation helpers
- migration CLI alpha available
- E2E tests for schema modes + tokenization edge-cases added to CI
- telemetry: schema_rejections, schema_fixups, x-rw-schema-status header on responses
- canary plan and rollback documented

rafa: engineering note: need to update routing layer to attach tenant flags early so we can enforce pinned_system before any user-supplied system message is processed. also ensure private deployment has an admin API to set pinned_system without exposing to app owners.

kevin (eng): security note: pinned system content should go through content-scan and secret-scan in case tenants accidentally embed secrets. add a warning in console when content contains patterns.

ops-bot: scheduled job created: "schema-canary-healthcheck" (interval=5m) pending canary start.

elaine: OK next actions: @kevin open runtime ticket with clear error shape examples, @tom open SDK ticket + estimate, @nina draft BetaBank migration proposal, @rafa schedule infra-window for canary. tag me when tickets are up and we'll slot into sprint. thanks.
